questions.question: What happens to a catalyst during a chemical reaction?
options: It is completely consumed
It speeds up the reaction without being used up
It turns into a new product
It slows down the reaction

questions.question: Which statement best describes how catalysts work for different chemical reactions?
options: One single catalyst can speed up any reaction
Different reactions require specific catalysts
Catalysts only work on metal displacement reactions
All catalysts are liquids

questions.question: What term is given to biological catalysts that speed up chemical processes inside living cells?
options: Polymers
Alloys
Enzymes
Monomers

questions.question: Under what condition will a displacement reaction occur between a metal and a salt solution?
options: The solid metal must be less reactive than the metal in the salt
Both metals must have equal reactivity
The solid metal must be more reactive than the metal in the salt
The solution must be heated to boiling point

questions.question: What are the products when solid magnesium is added to copper sulfate solution?
options: Magnesium oxide and sulfur gas
Magnesium sulfate solution and solid copper
Copper oxide and magnesium sulfate
Magnesium copper alloy and water

questions.question: How can displacement reactions be used in a chemistry laboratory?
options: To measure the exact boiling point of water
To determine the relative position of a metal in the reactivity series
To convert non-metals into metals
To break down polymers into monomers

questions.question: What is a metal ore?
options: A pure block of metal found underground
A rock containing enough of a metal compound to be extracted
A synthetic material made from polymers
A mixture of ceramics and liquids

questions.question: Why can carbon be used to extract iron from iron ore?
options: Carbon is less reactive than iron
Carbon is more reactive than iron
Carbon melts at a lower temperature than iron
Carbon is a biological catalyst

questions.question: Which set of physical properties is typical for most metals?
options: Brittle, dull, and poor conductors of electricity
Soft, liquid at room temperature, and flexible
Good conductors of heat and electricity, malleable, and shiny
Low melting point, transparent, and non-conductive

questions.question: How do ceramics change when soft substances like clay are heated in a furnace?
options: They become flexible and rubbery
They melt into a liquid that never hardens
They become hard and brittle
They conduct electricity very easily

questions.question: What type of giant molecules form the basis of all plastic materials?
options: Metals
Polymers
Ceramics
Crystals

questions.question: What is an alloy?
options: A compound made of two non-metals
A pure chemical element
A mixture of elements containing at least one metal
A polymer chain linked by plasticisers

questions.question: Why are composite materials designed by combining two or more different materials?
options: To make the final material cheaper without changing its behavior
To create a new material with improved overall properties
To ensure the material can dissolve in water
To convert polymers back into monomers

questions.question: What are the small repeating units that join together to form a polymer chain called?
options: Enzymes
Alloys
Monomers
Catalysts

questions.question: Why do certain polymers have high melting points?
options: Their polymer chains are extremely short
Their long molecules are difficult to separate from each other
They contain water trapped between the molecules
They are made entirely of metal atoms

questions.question: What is the main effect of adding a plasticiser to a polymer?
options: It creates strong cross-links between chains
It makes the polymer harder and more brittle
It gets between polymer molecules allowing them to slide over each other more easily
It causes the polymer to evaporate immediately

questions.question: What effect do cross-links between polymer chains have on the material's properties?
options: They make the polymer softer and more flexible
They make the polymer harder and less flexible
They lower the melting point drastically
They make the polymer soluble in water

questions.question: What products are formed when a metal reacts with an acid?
options: Metal hydroxide and oxygen gas
Metal salt and hydrogen gas
Metal oxide and carbon dioxide gas
Water and nitrogen gas

questions.question: Which two products are formed when a reactive metal reacts with cold water?
options: Metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas
Metal oxide and carbon dioxide gas
Metal salt and oxygen gas
Metal chloride and water

questions.question: What does a metal's higher position in the reactivity series indicate about its chemical behavior?
options: It reacts less vigorously with other substances
It is less likely to form compounds
It reacts more vigorously with other substances
It cannot displace any other metal
